knowledgePoint.title: Finding the Equation of a Circle Given the Center and the Radius

data.markdown:
![](images/ae/ae44c9f19c7afc26c399999105b7d17c6e2e6b3e020e7b419065a8514741dc9b.png)

 

Consider a circle with radius $3$ centered at the point $(3,0),$ shown above.

Write the equation of this circle in the form $(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.$

                            
                                    
                                        
                                            

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-1}}
data.solution:
The equation of a circle with radius $r$  centered at the point $(a,b)$ in rectangular coordinates in standard form is

$$
(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

In our case, the circle is centered at $(3,0)$ and the radius of the circle is $r=3$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ (x-3)^{2}+(y-0)^{2} & ={3}^{2} \\ (x-3)^{2}+{y}^{2} & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the equation of the circle in rectangular coordinates is 

$$
(x-3)^{2}+{y}^{2}=9.
$$
data.title: Finding the Equation of a Circle Given the Center and the Radius

Consider a circle with radius $6$ centered at the point $(0,6),$ shown above.

Write the equation of this circle in the form $(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.$

{{field-1}}
data.solution:
The equation of a circle with radius $r$  centered at the point $(a,b)$ in rectangular coordinates in standard form is

$$
(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

In our case, the circle is centered at $(0,6)$ and the radius of the circle is $r=6$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ (x-0)^{2}+(y-6)^{2} & ={6}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+(y-6)^{2} & =36.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the equation of the circle in rectangular coordinates is 

$$
{x}^{2}+(y-6)^{2}=36.
$$
